SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
JOHN hilburn’s INITIAL brief
John Hilburn files this Initial Brief in the above-styled and numbered docket. The intervenor number for this landowner is 317.  
In summary, my property is on Link G32, G2, G6 and I am opposed to any route that uses Link G32, G2, or G6 for the reasons set forth below.
Nineteen landowners on Link G2 filed written testimony that was admitted into evidence. This is an extremely high percentage of the properties affected by Link G2. This alone is strong evidence of the opposition to Link G2 by our rural community.
But there are more substantive reasons that Link G32, G2, and G6 should not be used:
Based on the testimony given on Tuesday, 06/09/2026, by Mr. Pool concerning the gas transmission terminal in Permian basin and his revisiting the necessity of the transmission lines, I would like to add the availability of Small Modular Reactors: Project Pele – micro reactors for remote military bases, Radiant, E Vinci, and Xenergy & Terra Power plan to be on grid late 2020s or early 2030s as better solutions than the proposed transmission lines.
The proposed G32 line is projected to bisect my land and go directly over my 3 BR 2 Bath mobile home with fresh water well and septic system, my stock tank, and is about 300 yds from my sheet metal barn and gates, stock pens, loading ramp and squeeze.
There are known health issues associated with living under high voltage transmission lines. There will be signal interference for TV, radio, and telephones. The mobile home can’t be moved without having to drill a new well, create a new septic system, and run necessary power lines. There will be health issues for people and animals at the barn. Also the barn being metal and having metal fences and gates, the energy field associated with the transmission lines can build up electric discharge to the metal structures.
There are three proposed transmission lines G32, G2, and G6. G32 cuts across my property to join G2 and G6 along the edge of my property. This would create a “Y” of transmission lines near my trailer house and over the metal gate entrance onto my property. Due to the associated energy field from the transmission lines my metal gate could become hazardous.
Due to known droughts and dry seasons, fire is a very possible occurrence.
 Common Causes for Fire:
Tornado Damage: When tornadoes snap high-voltage transmission towers or poles, the severed lines can spark fires upon contact with vegetation or structures.
Line Interaction: Downed power lines, or "power flashes," often occur during storms when lines touch or debris causes short circuits.
Wind & Dry Conditions: As noted in Iowa, high-wind events, even without a direct tornado hit, can break poles, and the high winds can quickly spread fires ignited by the damaged lines.
These events underscore the severe damage and fire hazards created when extreme weather impacts critical electrical transmission infrastructure. 
I have intentionally left my property natural. I have witnessed honeybees migrating (swarm) 3 times across my land. Twice I have been standing in millions of Monarch butterflies that have stopped on my property during migration. I have seen:
 Golden-cheeked Warblers - a federal endangered migratory songbird that nests exclusively in mature Ashe juniper-oak woodlands
Whooping Crane – federal endangered migratory birds have stopped in my stock tank during migration.
Texas Horned Lizard known locally as the "horny toad," this species is protected as threatened in Texas.
Migratory Birds: All hawks and owls are protected by federal and state laws.
Habitat Conservation: Burnet County includes areas that are critical habitats for the Golden-cheeked Warbler or requires mitigation in areas with mature Ashe juniper ("cedar") trees.
I believe that the proposed Transmission line will adversely change their habitat environment.
This property was purchased to create a natural nature retreat for my family and friends. A place to get away from all the city development infrastructure, hustle and bustle. No high voltage transmission line has ever been removed. They have only been updated and expanded. Once they are in place, all the negative effects are forever, generations. There is a finite amount of land. More land cannot be created once it is given up for the auspices of growth.
Based on the testimony given on Tuesday06/09/2026, by Mr. Pool, the transmission lines will not serve the public along its route. Both ends will be privately owned (Oncore and LCRA Transmission). That indicates that it is a private transmission line. According to the State of Texas Landowner’s Bill of Rights created by the Texas Attorney General:
“Private property may only be taken by a governmental entity or private entity that is authorized by law to do so. Your property may be taken only for a public purpose. That means it can only be taken for a purpose or use that serves the general public. Texas law prohibits condemnation authorities from taking your property to enhance tax revenues or foster economic development”.
 Therefore, this project should not qualify for Eminent domain.
If the transmission lines should be approved; to fairly compensate the landowners, a requirement for the approval of the project to Oncore and LCRA Transmission should be to create a series of preferred shares that guarantee a 40% tax free annual dividend payable monthly or quarterly. The share price will be pinned to Sempra’s, the majority owner of Oncore, share price. The shares will be tied to the land and will not be sellable for the duration the transmission line is in place. These shares will be used as compensation for the landowners. If the transmission line is removed and the land is to be returned to the landowner, the shares will be returned to the transmission line owner(s) as payment in full.
In conclusion, for the reasons stated above, I oppose any route using Link G32, G2, and G6.
Respectfully submitted,
John Hilburn
